headline: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets
dek: According to the Guardian and Engadget, the filing accuses Apple of pressuring suppliers.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The lawsuit
body: OpenAI countersued Apple over alleged trade secret theft (The Guardian, Engadget).
The filing also says Apple pressures hardware suppliers, and it was made in California.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What OpenAI alleges
s3.body: The company describes a former employee rehired by Apple.

points.t: He had access to plans for an unreleased device (The Guardian, Engadget).
OpenAI says he carried the information back to Apple (The Guardian).
Apple allegedly encourages files on personal accounts (Engadget).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Apple's response
body: Apple denies the claims and calls the filing a distraction (The Guardian).
The suit answers one Apple itself filed against OpenAI in July.

items.t: Neither suit has a court ruling yet (The Guardian, Engadget).
The ChatGPT integration on iPhone remains in place (Engadget).
Both firms compete in AI devices (The Guardian).

caption.hook: OpenAI countersues Apple and accuses it of trade secret theft.
body: According to the Guardian and Engadget, the filing was made in federal court in California and says Apple pressured hardware suppliers not to work with OpenAI. The company also claims Apple rehired a former employee who allegedly carried plans for a new device back to Apple.

Apple denies the claims and calls the filing an attempt to distract from the case it opened itself in July (The Guardian). Neither case has a ruling, and the ChatGPT partnership on iPhone continues (Engadget). The full story is at the link in bio.
caption.cta: Should hiring between rival AI companies come with stricter limits?
